metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–2% of recent mean or spike magnitude.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often over-anticipates decline; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.5) over 3+ days, model under-responds to downward pressure; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to forecast.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is > 5% above recent 10d average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30d horizon, model often misses late-cycle corrections; add 0.5–1.0% downward adjustment if sentiment turns negative after peak.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +0.7, -0.5, +0.7), model overfits to recent sentiment; dampen forecast by 10–15% if sentiment is “reversing” or “neutralizing”.
